intent: Implement the first independent Go desktop report workflow: create/select member, choose a local file, real PDFKit/Vision extraction, raw-and-corrected review, explicit confirmation, member-scoped search, and reopen durable records. Preserve the Swift baseline, use a separate sandbox identity/root, and distinguish current preview evidence from deferred functions and manual gates.

evidence: internal/library/store.go:183-192: On the next Open, databaseExists routes the zero-version file through the version/application check and returns ErrUnsupported.
internal/library/store.go:202-213: Schema initialization is a later transaction; its errors return without removing or recovering the newly created database.
findings.suggested_fix: Make first-run schema publication recoverable: initialize and sync a private temporary SQLite database, then atomically publish it as library.sqlite, or explicitly recognize and reinitialize only an app-created, empty version-zero database after validating that it has no user tables or originals. Add a restart test for interruption between file creation and schema commit.
findings.title: Interrupted first launch leaves library unable to reopen
findings.why_it_matters: A crash or storage error after creating library.sqlite but before the schema transaction commits leaves a version-zero database. Every later launch treats it as an unsupported format, so restarting cannot repair an otherwise empty preview library and the app cannot open.
findings.validation_reason: On a first launch interrupted after library.sqlite is created at internal/library/store.go:160 but before the schema transaction commits at 202-213, the next Open takes the existing-database branch at 183-193 and rejects its zero version/application ID; that interruption is reachable, though its incidence was not measured.

findings.first_evidence: internal/desktop/desktop.go:91 -- s.win.Update(func() { s.leave(func() { s.allowClose = true; s.stop(); mygo.App.Quit() }) })
findings.suggested_fix: Give window close and OnBeforeQuit a dedicated shutdown request path. For an active cancellable job, remember the close request, cancel jobCancel, and finish closing after that job settles; for a non-cancellable save, remember the request and wait for it to settle. Preserve the existing dirty-review save/discard/cancel handling before closing, and keep Service.Close responsible for waiting for native work and closing storage. Add a focused test that requests quit during the first file of a batch, verifies later files never start, and verifies the pending quit resumes after cleanup.
findings.title: Quitting during import leaves the entire batch running
findings.why_it_matters: Closing the window or choosing Quit during a multi-file import does not cancel recognition or queue a quit: it only displays the busy message, and all remaining files continue importing. Both close handlers route through the navigation guard, which returns whenever a job is active, so the shutdown cancellation in Service.Close is unreachable until the user separately cancels or waits for the batch and requests quit again. A dedicated close flow can cancel the active import, await its existing cleanup, and then finish quitting without requiring hard interruption of an Apple API.
findings.validation_reason: When close or Quit arrives during an import job, internal/desktop/desktop.go:77-91 calls leave, whose busy branch at 196-200 neither cancels jobCancel nor retains the close request, so the batch loop at 383-400 continues until a separate cancellation; the ordering is reachable through the chooser and incidence was not measured.

evidence: internal/library/store.go:394-407: The exclusive .part file is created and written; this error branch returns ErrStorage without removing it.
internal/library/store.go:393-416: No deferred removal covers cancellation or Link failure; directory sync occurs only after the temporary name was removed.
findings.suggested_fix: After creating the .part file, defer a best-effort removal of that temporary name on every exit path, disabling it only after successful removal; keep the separately published .blob behavior unchanged. Add a write/sync failure test that confirms no .part remains.
findings.title: Failed original writes retain partial files
findings.why_it_matters: When a write, sync, or close fails, the incomplete <id>.part file remains in originals. Repeating imports after disk pressure or another transient I/O failure accumulates unreachable files, consumes more space, and can keep subsequent imports failing. The preview has no cleanup path for these files.
findings.validation_reason: If a created original's write, sync, close, cancellation check, or link fails, internal/library/store.go:393-416 returns without removing its .part file, while the documented preservation of published orphan blobs does not cover this incomplete temporary file; failure incidence was not measured.

findings.first_evidence: internal/library/store.go:593: 	rows, err := s.db.QueryContext(ctx, "SELECT "+reportColumns+" FROM reports "+clause, args...)
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a lightweight report-list DTO and query only ID, display name/title, date, status, and created time for list views; keep full extraction loading in Get for the selected report. Page the timeline/search results and render only the current page or visible rows. Verify a large synthetic library's load time and peak memory.
findings.title: Timeline loads every full report into memory
findings.why_it_matters: Opening a member timeline or refreshing after an import, save, or search reads every matching report, including up to 1 MiB of corrected text and up to 2 MiB of extraction JSON per report. The store decodes and validates every extraction, retains all reports in a slice, and the UI builds a control for every item. A household library with hundreds of reports can therefore cause large allocation spikes and slow timeline loads even though the list displays only title, date, and status.
findings.validation_reason: For a member with many large confirmed reports, internal/library/store.go:431-445,592-629 selects and decodes full text and extraction for every unbounded result, internal/desktop/desktop.go:150-163 retains the result, and view.go:143-168 constructs a control per row; large-library incidence and peak allocations were not measured.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a generated image-only PDF test with a legible synthetic text image. Call Extract on the PDF and assert Kind=pdf, the correct page number, Method=vision, and a recognizable text anchor; include a mixed text/scanned two-page case if the fixture can stay small.
findings.title: Exercise scanned PDF recognition in native tests
findings.why_it_matters: A scanned PDF is a normal report input, but the new native tests exercise only the PDF text-layer branch and Vision on a standalone PNG. The PDF-to-raster-to-Vision branch could fail or lose page provenance while all current tests pass, leaving scanned reports without usable candidates.
findings.validation_reason: An image-only PDF reaches renderPDF then recognize at internal/macos/document_darwin.go:52-63, but native_darwin_test.go:63-92 asserts only PDF text-layer extraction and 115-139 asserts Vision only after converting a rendered page to standalone PNG, so no native test checks scanned-PDF Vision output or page provenance.
